newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans see Kohl place in history as Europe leader.
newsitem.headline: Germans see Kohl place in history as Europe leader.

text.p: Germans believe Chancellor Helmut Kohl is more interested in European affairs than domestic issues and that his efforts to unite Europe will be his primary mark in history, an opinion poll published on Friday found.

As Kohl shapes up to become Germany's longest-serving chancellor this century, 79 percent of Germans surveyed by the Emnid institute for the television network N-TV said his main achievement had been pushing for European integration.
A slightly smaller number, 74 percent, said Kohl's effort to unite East and West Germany in 1990 would go down in history as his main success in his 14 years in office.

But respondents rated Kohl as only the sixth most important 20th century politician, after former U.S. president John F. Kennedy, former chancellor Konrad Adenauer, ex-Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, "chancellor of detente" Willy Brandt and South African President Nelson Mandela.
Kohl will pass Adenauer as the longest-serving chancellor this century at the end of October.

The survey found that only 26 percent thought Kohl had any special interest in environmental or social issues, 38 percent thought he deserved praise for domestic security and 40 percent believed he was a guarantee for a strong economy.
